title: January heat sums at a 5 C base had more date error for five English butterflies in four tests in 1995-2024
abstract: We tested whether daily heat sums improve later butterfly mean flight dates over monthly temperature. We used UKBMS 2024 records and E-OBS daily mean temperature v32.0e. Five summer species supplied 19,784 test records at 325 matched English sites. Separate northern and southern site sets were tested in 1995-2009 and 2010-2024 after 15 training years. The primary model summed heat above 5 C from January 1 and kept a fixed mean training heat requirement for each site and species. Its mean absolute error exceeded the monthly model by 3.38 and 4.77 days in the early south and north, and 0.63 and 0.84 days in the later samples. Three of four adjusted block-bootstrap ranges were above zero. A March start reduced early excess errors by 1.90 and 2.27 days, but did not establish a repeated gain over monthly temperature. Count filters, omission of 2020 and exclusion of substituted weather cells kept all four primary difference signs. These results limit this simple heat model. They do not reject other thermal models or show why real flight dates changed. Weather is observed after each year. Matched-site selection, incomplete visits, coarse weather and short test periods limit transfer. Uncertainty ranges hold training fits fixed. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, figures and independent checks are included; external data and record-level derivatives remain outside the signed package.
